extracted.intended_audience: World Factbook contributors, editors, and US government officials (and other users of the Factbook)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and data-definition guidelines for preparing and presenting country/area entries in the CIA World Factbook, including definitions of statistical entries, formatting rules for names and numbers, and selection criteria for content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial sea (UNCLOS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sovereignty of a coastal state extends beyond its land territory and internal waters to an adjacent belt of sea (territorial sea); sovereignty extends to the air space over the territorial sea as well as its underlying seabed and subsoil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every state has the right to establish the breadth of its territorial sea up to a limit not exceeding 12 nautical miles; the normal baseline for measuring the breadth is the low-water line along the coast as marked on large-scale charts officially recognized by the coastal state. UNCLOS contains specific rules for archipelagic states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contiguous zone (UNCLOS Article 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: A zone contiguous to a coastal state's territorial sea over which it may exercise control necessary to prevent/punish infringement of customs, fiscal, immigration, or sanitary laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contiguous zone may not extend beyond 24 nautical miles from the baselines from which the territorial sea is measured (example: US has claimed a 12-nautical mile contiguous zone in addition to its 12-nautical mile territorial sea).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) (UNCLOS Part V)
rubrics_metrics.description: A zone beyond and adjacent to the territorial sea in which a coastal state has sovereign rights for exploring, exploiting, conserving and managing natural resources of waters, seabed and subsoil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes jurisdiction over artificial islands, marine scientific research, and protection/preservation of the marine environment. Outer limit shall not exceed 200 nautical miles from baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continental shelf (UNCLOS Article 76)
rubrics_metrics.description: The seabed and subsoil of submarine areas that extend beyond the territorial sea throughout the natural prolongation of the land territory to the outer edge of the continental margin, or to 200 nautical miles where the margin doesn't extend that far.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the continental margin extends beyond 200 nm, claims may extend to a distance not to exceed 350 nautical miles or 100 nautical miles from the 2500 meter isobath; does not include deep ocean floor and oceanic ridges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive fishing zone (non-UNCLOS term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Term used by some states (e.g., the UK) that choose not to claim an EEZ but claim jurisdiction over living resources off their coast; breadth normally same as EEZ (200 nm).

rubrics_metrics.name: Median age
rubrics_metrics.description: Age that divides a population into two numerically equal groups (half younger, half older); a single index summarizing age distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Age structure' for the importance of young versus older age structure and implications of low vs higher median age; current ranges cited (about 15 to 40+).

rubrics_metrics.name: Merchant marine – definition and fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Merchant marine defined as all ships engaged in carriage of goods or all commercial vessels (excluding tugs, fishing vessels, offshore oil rigs, etc.). Entry contains four fields: total, ships by type, foreign-owned, and registered in other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total includes number of ships (1,000 GRT or over), total DWT for those ships, and total GRT. DWT and GRT definitions provided; no stable relationship between GRT and DWT. Ships by type should list types (barge carriers, bulk cargo, container ships, tankers, passenger ships, etc.). Foreign-owned = fly one flag but owned by another country. Registered in other countries = belong to owners in one country but fly the flag of another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military – category scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Category includes entries dealing with a country's military structure, manpower, and expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military branches
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry lists names of the ground, naval, air, marine, and other defense or security forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military expenditures - dollar figure
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives current military expenditures in US dollars; calculated by multiplying estimated defense spending (percent) by GDP on an exchange rate basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dollar figures should be treated with caution because of different price patterns, accounting methods among nations, and variations in currency strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military expenditures - percent of GDP
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives current military expenditures as an estimated percent of gross domestic product (GDP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Military manpower - availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives total numbers of males and females age 15-49 and assumes every individual is fit to serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a broad measure of potential manpower availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military manpower - fit for military service
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives number of males and females age 15-49 fit for military service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A more refined measure accounting for the health situation to produce a more realistic estimate of those fit to serve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military manpower - military age
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives the minimum age at which an individual may volunteer for military service or be subject to conscription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military manpower - reaching military age annually
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives the number of draft-age males and females entering the military manpower pool each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a measure of availability of draft-age young adults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military - note
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry for miscellaneous military information of significance not included elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money figures – currency convention
rubrics_metrics.description: All money figures are expressed in contemporaneous US dollars unless otherwise indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: National holiday
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives the primary national day of celebration—usually independence day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides identifying terms for citizens—noun and adjective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas - production
rubrics_metrics.description: Total natural gas produced in cubic meters (cu m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrepancies between production/imports and consumption/exports may be due to omission of stock changes and other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas - consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Total natural gas consumed in cubic meters (cu m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrepancies may result from omission of stock changes and other complicating factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas - exports
rubrics_metrics.description: Total natural gas exported in cubic meters (cu m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas - imports
rubrics_metrics.description: Total natural gas imported in cubic meters (cu m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas - proved reserves
rubrics_metrics.description: Stock of proved reserves of natural gas in cubic meters (cu m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved reserves are quantities which, by analysis of geological and engineering data, can be estimated with a high degree of confidence to be commercially recoverable from a given date forward, from known reservoirs and under current economic conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural hazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists potential natural disasters relevant to the country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists a country's mineral, petroleum, hydropower, and other commercially important resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net migration rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Difference between number of persons entering and leaving a country during the year per 1,000 persons (based on midyear population).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive = net immigration; negative = net emigration. Indicates contribution of migration to population change. High levels of migration can cause problems (unemployment, potential ethnic strife) or reduce labor force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oil - production
rubrics_metrics.description: Total oil produced in barrels per day (bbl/day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrepancies between production/imports and consumption/exports may be due to omission of stock changes, refinery gains, and other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oil - consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Total oil consumed in barrels per day (bbl/day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrepancies may be due to omission of stock changes, refinery gains, and other complicating factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oil - exports
rubrics_metrics.description: Total oil exported in barrels per day (bbl/day), including crude and oil products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oil - imports
rubrics_metrics.description: Total oil imported in barrels per day (bbl/day), including crude and oil products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oil - proved reserves
rubrics_metrics.description: Stock of proved reserves of crude oil in barrels (bbl).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved reserves are quantities which, by analysis of geological and engineering data, can be estimated with a high degree of confidence to be commercially recoverable from a given date forward, from known reservoirs and under current economic conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: People – category scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Category includes entries dealing with characteristics of the people and their society.

rubrics_metrics.name: People - note
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry for miscellaneous demographic information of significance not included elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Names - Capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Factbook capitalizes the surname or family name of individuals for the convenience of users faced with different cultures and naming conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: MAO Zedong, Fidel CASTRO Ruz, George W. BUSH. Knowing the surname permits confident use of short forms (e.g., President Castro). System extended to leaders with surnames not commonly used (e.g., Queen ELIZABETH II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Names - Spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Romanization of personal names normally follows the US Board on Geographic Names transliteration system for place names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a foreign leader expressly indicates a preference, or media/official documents regularly use an alternative romanization, the Factbook uses that alternative spelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Names - Titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize any valid title (or short form of it) immediately preceding a person's name; a title standing alone is not capitalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: President PUTIN and President BUSH; note differences in chief of state/head of government across countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry gives the lengths and types of pipelines for transporting products like natural gas, crude oil, or petroleum products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political parties and leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry includes a listing of significant political organizations and their leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political pressure groups and leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry includes a listing of organizations with leaders involved in politics but not standing for legislative election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population - estimation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives an estimate from the US Bureau of the Census based on censuses, vital statistics registration systems, or sample surveys and on assumptions about future trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starting 1993 Factbook, demographic estimates for some countries have explicitly taken into account effects of HIV/AIDS epidemic; list of countries adjusted provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population below poverty line
rubrics_metrics.description: National estimates of percent of population falling below the poverty line are based on surveys of sub-groups weighted by group population size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions of poverty vary considerably among nations (rich nations generally use more generous standards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Population growth rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Average annual percent change in population resulting from surplus/deficit of births over deaths and net migration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate affects burden on infrastructure, resources, and jobs; rapid growth can be seen as threatening by neighbors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ports and harbors – selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists major ports and harbors selected on the basis of overall importance to each country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection determined by evaluating factors such as dollar value of goods handled, gross tonnage, facilities, and military significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public debt
rubrics_metrics.description: Records cumulative total of all government borrowings less repayments denominated in a country's home currency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should not be confused with external debt, which reflects foreign currency liabilities of private and public sector and must be financed out of foreign exchange earnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radio broadcast stations
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry includes total number of AM, FM, and shortwave broadcast stations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railways
rubrics_metrics.description: States total route length of the railway network and component parts by gauge: broad, standard, narrow, and dual; other gauges listed under note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Section includes world and regional maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refugees and internally displaced persons (IDPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry includes persons residing in a country as refugees or IDPs; provides UN Convention definition of refugee and UNRWA operational definition for Palestinian refugees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that 'internally displaced person' is not specifically covered in UN Convention and that UNHCR estimates global refugee and IDP populations; examples and distinctions provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordered listing of religions by adherents starting with the largest group and sometimes includes percent of total population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserves of foreign exchange and gold
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives dollar value for stock of all financial assets available to the central monetary authority for meeting balance of payments needs as of period end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes foreign currency, gold, Special Drawing Rights (IMF), and a country's reserve position in the Fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes number of males for each female in five age groups (at birth, under 15, 15-64, 65+, and total population).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sex ratio at birth is an indicator of certain kinds of sex discrimination (e.g., sex-selective abortion, infanticide) and has long-term social implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suffrage
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives the age at enfranchisement and whether the right to vote is universal or restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone numbers – formatting convention
rubrics_metrics.description: All telephone numbers consist of the country code in brackets, the city or area code (where required) in parentheses, and the local number; international access code is not presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: From US to Madrid: 011 [34] (1) 577-xxxx. From another country to US: international access code + [1] (202) 939-xxxx.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone system – descriptive scope and terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry includes a brief general assessment of the telephone system with details on domestic and international components and uses defined terms/abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides definitions for many terms and abbreviations (e.g., Africa ONE, Arabsat, Autodin, CB, cellular telephone system, coaxial cable, fiber-optic cable, GSM, HF, Inmarsat, Intelsat, landline, microwave radio relay, satellite earth station, UHF, VHF, submarine cable, etc.) to ensure consistent use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephones - main lines in use
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives the total number of main telephone lines in use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephones - mobile cellular
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives the total number of mobile cellular telephones in use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television - broadcast stations
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives the total number of separate broadcast stations plus any repeater stations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology – use of collective generic terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to the structured database, collective generic terms are used (e.g., 'Country' refers to dependencies, areas of special sovereignty, uninhabited islands, etc.; 'Military' used as umbrella term for civil defense, security activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence entry may include traditional founding/unification or state succession dates; dependent areas have dependency status noted in same entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terrain
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry contains a brief description of the topography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total fertility rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Average number of children that would be born per woman if she lived through childbearing years and bore children according to given age-specific fertility rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More direct measure of fertility than crude birth rate; indicates potential for population growth and implications for labor force participation and family resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transnational Issues – scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Category includes entries that deal with current issues beyond national boundaries (currently Disputes - international and Illicit drugs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation – category scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes entries dealing with means for movement of people and goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation - note
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry includes miscellaneous transportation information of significance not included elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unemployment rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of the labor force that is without jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial underemployment might be noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waterways
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives the total length of navigable rivers, canals, and other inland bodies of water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Years – date conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: All year references are for the calendar year (CY) unless indicated as fiscal year (FY).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calendar year is 1 January to 31 December; fiscal year is an accounting period other than calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligence Cycle and finished intelligence types
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines Information, Intelligence, Finished intelligence and describes three types of finished intelligence: basic, current, and estimative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic intelligence provides fundamental factual reference material (e.g., World Factbook); current intelligence reports new developments; estimative intelligence judges probable outcomes. The three are mutually supportive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributors and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Factbook is prepared by the CIA for US Government use; information provided by multiple US government agencies and other public/private sources; edition uses information available as of 1 January 2004.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style, format, coverage and content are designed to meet specific US government requirements; contributor list and public-domain status described; CIA seal not to be copied without permission.
